info.title: Strombauer Shopware API
info.description:
API of the Strombauer shop for apps and integrations. All paths start with `/store-api/v1/`.

## Headers

- `sw-access-key`: required for every request. This documentation sets it automatically.
- `sw-context-token`: identifies the session. Endpoints that require the `ContextToken` scheme need a logged-in customer: log in with `POST /store-api/v1/account/login` and send the returned token with every following request. If a response contains a new `sw-context-token` header, use it from then on. To test requests here, run `POST /store-api/v1/account/login` with e-mail and password (Swagger UI: login in the *Authorize* dialog); the token is then stored and sent automatically.

## Registration flow

1. Check the e-mail address: `POST /store-api/v1/account/email-check`. With `mode: login` the customer already exists, continue with `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`. With `mode: register` continue with step 2.
2. Register the company: `POST /store-api/v1/account/business-register`. The country of the billing address comes from `GET /store-api/v1/country`. The response header `sw-context-token` contains the token of the now logged-in customer.
3. Load free slots for the onboarding call: `GET /store-api/v1/onboarding/booking-slots`
4. Book the onboarding call: `POST /store-api/v1/onboarding/booking` with `start` of the chosen slot as `appointmentStart`.

Prices and ordering are unlocked after the onboarding call.

## Passkey login

1. Get the request options: `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/login-options`. After the user entered the e-mail address (`POST /store-api/v1/account/email-check` answered `mode: login`), send it as `email`: `publicOptions.allowCredentials` then lists only the passkeys of that account. If the list is empty, continue with the password login.
2. Pass `publicOptions` to the passkey API of the platform and send the result with `ceremonyId` to `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/login`. The response header `sw-context-token` contains the token of the logged-in customer.

To add a passkey, the logged-in customer confirms the password with `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/register-options` and the result of the platform goes to `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/register`.

Every address has its own passkeys. Apps send no `rpId` and use the shop address. A web shop on its own address sends it as `rpId` to both options endpoints; its passkeys only work there.

## Forgotten password

1. Request the mail: `POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password` with the e-mail address. The mail contains a link to the shop: `https://shop.strombauer.com/account/recover/password?hash=…`.
2. Optional: check the `hash` of the link with `POST /store-api/v1/account/customer-recovery-is-expired` to show an expired link right away.
3. Set the new password: `POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password-confirm` with `hash`, `newPassword` and `newPasswordConfirm`. All sessions of the customer end; continue with `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`.

A link is valid for 2 hours and only once. Requesting a new mail makes the previous link invalid. Treat the hash like a password: do not log it, do not pass it to analytics or tracking.

## Account activation

An inactive account is activated with the link of its activation mail. The link points to the shop: `https://shop.strombauer.com/showactivatecustomer/{code}`. On that page the customer sets the first password and accepts the terms and conditions; send both with the code as `hash` to `POST /store-api/v1/account/activate`. The response header `sw-context-token` contains the token of the now logged-in customer.

The code works only once. Treat it like a password: do not log it, do not pass it to analytics or tracking.

## Order flow

1. Log in: `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`
2. Find products: `GET /store-api/v1/product` or `GET /store-api/v1/search`
3. Fill the cart: `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/cart/line-item`
4. Choose shipping and payment with the endpoints of the *Checkout* group. The allowed values are listed in the cart under `available`.
5. Place the order: `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order`
6. Follow the order in `GET /store-api/v1/sales-orders`; until it is listed, usually within a few minutes, `pendingOrderCount` counts it.

Instead of steps 4 and 5, the customer can send the cart as a quote request: `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/quote-request`.

Prices and stock come only for customers that are unlocked for orders. Guests and logged-in customers of a locked customer group (e.g. „Blockiert“) get the same product data: `calculatedPrice` is empty (`[]`), `availableStock` and `stockForecast` are `null`, `price` is not offered as sort order, and stored carts come without prices (`available: false`). Show ordering only when a product has a price. Adding a product as a locked customer answers `403` with `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_PURCHASE_NOT_ALLOWED`; a cart filled before the lock keeps its positions, shows a notice with this code and the order is rejected with it (`400`). `GET /store-api/v1/account/customer` carries `customerState` (`LOCKED`, `UNLOCKED`); together with the session (none = guest) it tells the three cases apart.

## Search and clicks

1. Search with `GET /store-api/v1/search`: `source=suggest` for every request of a preview while typing, `source=results` for the result page. Keep `searchLogId` of the first page. Searches the user did not type (e.g. looking up item numbers) go without `source`; they are not recorded and `searchLogId` is `null`.
2. When the user opens a product of the result or adds it to the cart from there: `POST /store-api/v1/search-log/click/{searchLogId}`.

Send the same `sw-context-token` with all searches and clicks of a visit.

## Errors

Every error response has the same format, a list with one entry per error:

```json
{"errors": [{"status": "400", "code": "VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR", "detail": "Bitte gib die Telefonnummer an.", "source": {"pointer": "/phoneNumber"}}]}
```

- `status`: HTTP status as a string.
- `code`: stable, machine-readable error code. Apps decide by `code`, never by `detail`.
- `detail`: German sentence for the customer, addressed with "du". It never contains codes, IDs, English texts or other internals and can be shown as it is.
- `source.pointer`: the field the error belongs to, e.g. `/phoneNumber` or `/billingAddress/street`; postal code errors use `/zipcode`. `source` is left out when the error belongs to no field.

A missing login always answers `401` with `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_LOGIN_REQUIRED` (detail "Bitte melde dich an."), on every endpoint that needs a logged-in customer (also for guests). A wrong e-mail address or password at the login stays `401` `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_AUTH_BAD_CREDENTIALS`.

In this documentation `CODE/field` (e.g. `VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/street`) stands for an error with this `code` and the `source.pointer` `/street`. `409` `CHECKOUT__CART_LOCKED` means the cart is being changed by another request; send the request again shortly.

Search parameters: `GET /product`, `GET /product/{productId}`, `GET /search`, `GET /category`, `GET /manufacturers`, `GET /country` and `GET /account/customer` accept the parameters documented for them. For guests and customers without price access (not logged in, without customer number or in a locked customer group such as „Blockiert“), the search parameters `ids`, `term`, `sort`, `limit`, `page`, `filter`, `post-filter`, `query`, `grouping`, `aggregations`, `associations`, `fields`, `includes`, `excludes`, `total-count-mode` and `_criteria` return `400` `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__PARAMETER_NOT_ALLOWED/<parameter>` on these endpoints unless the endpoint lists them. The pointer names the first such parameter of the request.

post.summary: Activates an account with the link of the activation mail
post.description:
Activates an inactive account with the link of the activation mail and logs the customer in. Send the code from the link (`https://shop.strombauer.com/showactivatecustomer/{code}`) as `hash`. No login needed.

The customer sets the first password and has to accept the terms and conditions. The code works only once. The response is the same as for `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`: the header `sw-context-token` contains the token of the now logged-in customer.

The password needs at least 8 characters. Requests are limited per IP address, failed attempts count too (`429`).

hash.description: Code from the link of the activation mail, 32 hexadecimal characters.

password.description: First password of the account, at least 8 characters. Spaces alone do not count.

termsAccepted.description: Has to be `true`: the customer accepts the terms and conditions.

400.description:
Invalid input, the field is part of the code:

- `VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/password`: `password` is missing, empty or only spaces (`VIOLATION::INVALID_TYPE_ERROR/password` if it is not a string).
- `VIOLATION::TOO_SHORT_ERROR/password`: `password` has less than 8 characters.
- `VIOLATION::NOT_TRUE_ERROR/termsAccepted`: `termsAccepted` is missing or not `true`.

Several errors can be returned together. They are only checked for a valid code, otherwise the answer is `404`.

errors.detail: Das Passwort muss mindestens 8 Zeichen lang sein.
Bitte akzeptiere die AGB.

404.description: `STROMBAUER__ACTIVATION_HASH_INVALID`: the code is missing, malformed, unknown or already used. Show that the link is invalid.

errors.detail: Der Aktivierungslink ist ungültig oder wurde schon verwendet.

429.description: `FRAMEWORK__RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: too many attempts from this IP address. Try again later.

post.description:
Step 2 of the registration flow, after `POST /store-api/v1/account/email-check` answered `mode: register`. Creates a customer account. Send `multipart/form-data`; the business license (PDF) and the UTM parameters are optional. Take `billingAddress[countryId]` from `GET /store-api/v1/country`.

The customer is logged in right away: use the `sw-context-token` from the response header for the next steps.

email.description: E-mail address, also the login name.

acceptedDataProtection.description: Privacy policy and terms accepted. Must be `true` (`1` in multipart).

billingAddress[phoneNumber].description: Phone number, used for the onboarding call.

billingAddress[mobile].description: Optional mobile number, maximum 20 characters (digits, spaces, `+`, `-`, `/`, `(`, `)`). Returned as `mobile` by `GET /store-api/v1/account/customer`.

billingAddress[countryId].description: Country ID from `GET /store-api/v1/country`. A billing address in an EU country other than Germany needs a VAT ID of that country in `vatIds[]` (AG-732).

vatIds[].description: VAT IDs of the company, one field per VAT ID. Required for a billing address in an EU country other than Germany: at least one VAT ID must belong to that country (e.g. `ATU12345678` for Austria; spaces, dots and hyphens are ignored), otherwise `VIOLATION::VAT_ID_OF_BILLING_COUNTRY_MISSING/vatIds`. Optional for Germany.

businessLicense.description: Optional business license (Gewerbenachweis) as PDF, maximum 10 MB.

registrationAttribution.description: Optional UTM parameters the user arrived with, as JSON object string: `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`, `utm_term`, `utm_id` (each max. 255 characters, other keys are ignored). Only send them if the user consented to tracking.

204.description: Customer registered and logged in. No body, the header `sw-context-token` contains the token.

sw-context-token.description: Token of the logged-in customer. Send it as `sw-context-token` with `GET /store-api/v1/onboarding/booking-slots` and `POST /store-api/v1/onboarding/booking`.

400.description: Invalid registration fields or business license. Validation errors append the field to the code. `VIOLATION::VAT_ID_OF_BILLING_COUNTRY_MISSING/vatIds`: the billing address is in an EU country other than Germany and none of the VAT IDs belongs to that country (AG-732); ask for the VAT ID of the billing country or a billing address in Germany.

errors.detail: Bitte gib die Straße und Hausnummer an.
Zu dieser E-Mail-Adresse gibt es schon ein Konto. Bitte melde dich an.

429.description: More than 10 registration attempts from this IP address within one hour, failed attempts included. Wait the given seconds.

errors.detail: Zu viele Anfragen. Bitte warte einen Moment und versuche es dann noch einmal.

post.description:
Changes the password of the logged-in customer. The customer confirms the current password and enters the new one twice.

After the change all other sessions of the customer end, on every device and in every app. The current session stays logged in, but under a new token: replace the stored `sw-context-token` with the one from the response header, the previous token no longer works. The customer gets an e-mail that the password was changed.

The new password needs at least 8 characters. At most 5 attempts per hour and customer, wrong passwords and invalid input count too; a successful change resets the counter (`429`).

An account without a password (login only by passkey) cannot confirm a current password and gets `409`. Send the customer to the forgotten password flow (`POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password`) to set one.

newPasswordConfirm.description: Repetition of the new password, has to be equal to `newPassword`.

400.description:
Invalid input, the field is part of the code:

- `VIOLATION::CUSTOMER_PASSWORD_NOT_CORRECT/password`: the current password is wrong or missing.
- `VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/newPassword`: `newPassword` is missing or empty.
- `VIOLATION::TOO_SHORT_ERROR/newPassword`: `newPassword` has less than 8 characters.
- `VIOLATION::NOT_EQUAL_ERROR/newPasswordConfirm`: `newPasswordConfirm` differs from `newPassword`; checked first, other errors are then not reported.

Several errors can be returned together.

400.description: Guests and customers without price access sent a search parameter, e.g. `filter` or `limit` (`source.pointer` is the parameter).

post.summary: Checks the link of the recovery mail
post.description:
Optional step of the password reset: checks the `hash` from the link of the recovery mail before the form is shown, so an expired link is visible right away. No login needed. The password is set with `POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password-confirm`, which checks the hash again.

A link is valid for 2 hours. Requests that send a hash are limited per IP address together with `POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password-confirm` (`429`).

hash.description: Value of the parameter `hash` from the link in the recovery mail, 32 characters.

200.description: The link exists. `isExpired: true` means it is older than 2 hours.

400.description: `hash` is missing (`VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/hash`), not a string (`VIOLATION::INVALID_TYPE_ERROR/hash`) or not 32 characters long (`VIOLATION::NOT_EQUAL_LENGTH_ERROR/hash`).

404.description: `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND_BY_HASH`: the link is unknown, already used or replaced by a newer mail. Treat it like an expired link.

post.summary: Check e-mail for login or registration
post.description:
Step 1 of the registration flow. Tells whether a customer account exists for the e-mail address: `mode: login` continues with `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`, `mode: register` with `POST /store-api/v1/account/business-register`. An invalid address answers `valid: false` and `mode: null`.

At most 30 requests per minute and IP address, otherwise `429`.

200.description: Next step for the e-mail address.

valid.description: The e-mail address is syntactically valid.

mode.description: `login` for an existing customer, `register` for a new one, `null` for an invalid address.

post.description: Logs in with the e-mail address and password of the shop account. The response header `sw-context-token` identifies the session; send it with every request that needs a login.

username.description: E-mail address of the shop account.

errors.detail: Bitte melde dich an.

post.description:
Step 2 of the passkey login. Verifies the passkey assertion and logs the customer in. Answers like `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`: the header `sw-context-token` carries the token of the logged-in customer. A `ceremonyId` can be used only once. The address (`rpId`) comes from the ceremony: only passkeys created for that address are accepted, from the origin `https://<rpId>`. If the options were requested with the `email` of an account, only a passkey of that account is accepted.

Every failure answers `401` with `PASSKEY__LOGIN_FAILED`, whether the passkey is unknown, belongs to another address or to another account than the requested `email`, the signature is invalid, the ceremony expired or the customer is inactive. Start again with `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/login-options`.

400.description: `ceremonyId` or `credential` is missing or too large.

401.description: The passkey login failed.

errors.detail: Die Anmeldung mit dem Passkey ist fehlgeschlagen.

404.description: Passkey login is not available in this shop (`PASSKEY__DISABLED`).

post.description:
Step 1 of the passkey login. Returns WebAuthn request options. Pass `publicOptions` to the platform passkey API (iOS `ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider`, Android Credential Manager, browser `navigator.credentials.get()`) and send the result with `ceremonyId` to `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/login` within 5 minutes.

Passkeys are bound to an address (`rpId`). Without a body the options are for the shop address (e.g. `shop.strombauer.com`): passkeys created in the shop also work in the apps, which must be linked to this domain (iOS Associated Domains, Android Digital Asset Links). A web shop on its own address sends it as `rpId` and gets its own passkeys, valid only there; the origin of the browser must be `https://<rpId>`. Only the addresses enabled for this shop are accepted, others answer `400`.

Without `email` the options are for any passkey of the address (discoverable passkeys), `allowCredentials` is empty. With `email` (e.g. after `POST /store-api/v1/account/email-check` answered `mode: login`) the login is bound to that account: `publicOptions.allowCredentials` lists its passkeys for the address, each with `type`, `id` (base64url) and `transports` if known, so the browser offers only these. An account without passkeys for the address, an unknown e-mail address and an inactive account all get an empty list; then continue with the password login (`POST /store-api/v1/account/login`). The e-mail address is compared like in the login (case-insensitive, surrounding spaces removed); an invalid address answers `400`.

At most 10 requests per minute and IP address, with or without `email`, otherwise `429`.

200.description: Request options and the ID of the ceremony.

withoutEmail.summary: Any passkey of the shop address

withEmail.summary: Passkeys of the account for the web shop

400.description: `rpId` is not an address enabled for this shop, or `email` is not a valid e-mail address.

errors.detail: Passkeys stehen hier nicht zur Verfügung.
Die E-Mail-Adresse ist ungültig.

post.description: Step 2 of adding a passkey. Verifies the authenticator response and stores the passkey for the logged-in customer and the address (`rpId`) of the ceremony; the response must come from the origin `https://<rpId>`. The label is generated from the `User-Agent` header and the language of the context. A `ceremonyId` can be used only once and only by the customer who started it.

400.description: The ceremony expired or was already used (`PASSKEY__CEREMONY_UNAVAILABLE`, start again), or the authenticator response is invalid (`PASSKEY__REGISTRATION_FAILED`).

errors.detail: Der Vorgang ist abgelaufen. Bitte starte ihn erneut.

401.description: No customer is logged in (`CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_LOGIN_REQUIRED`).

404.description: Passkey login is not available in this shop (`PASSKEY__DISABLED`).

post.description:
Step 1 of adding a passkey. Confirms the current password of the logged-in customer and returns WebAuthn creation options. Pass `publicOptions` to the platform passkey API (browser `navigator.credentials.create()`) and send the result with `ceremonyId` to `POST /store-api/v1/account/passkey/register` within 5 minutes.

Without `rpId` the passkey is for the shop address (shop and apps). A web shop on its own address sends it as `rpId`; the passkey then works only there. `excludeCredentials` lists the customer's passkeys of the same address, passkeys of other addresses do not block a new one. Only the addresses enabled for this shop are accepted, others answer `400` before the password is checked.

At most 10 requests per minute and customer, and at most 5 password attempts per hour and customer (a correct password resets them), otherwise `429`.

rpId.description: Address of the web shop the passkey is for, without scheme, e.g. `newshop.strombauer.com`. Omit it for the shop address.

200.description: Creation options and the ID of the ceremony.

400.description: `password` is missing, `rpId` is not an address enabled for this shop (`PASSKEY__RELYING_PARTY_NOT_ALLOWED`), or the options could not be created (`PASSKEY__REGISTRATION_FAILED`).

errors.detail: Passkeys stehen hier nicht zur Verfügung.

401.description: The password is wrong (`PASSKEY__WRONG_PASSWORD`), or no customer is logged in (`CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_LOGIN_REQUIRED`).

errors.detail: Das Passwort ist nicht korrekt.
Bitte melde dich an.

429.description: Too many attempts of this customer (`FRAMEWORK__RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).

post.description:
Step 1 of the password reset: sends a password recovery mail. The link in the mail opens the reset page of the shop (`https://shop.strombauer.com/account/recover/password?hash=…`). The reset page continues with `POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password-confirm`.

Only `email` is required. The answer is the same whether an account exists or not. Requests are limited per e-mail address and IP address (`429`).

email.description: E-Mail address to identify the customer

storefrontUrl.description: Optional. Domain of the link in the mail, it has to be a domain of the shop. Default: `https://shop.strombauer.com`.

200.description: If email corresponds to an existing customer, a recovery mail is sent. Returns a success indicating a successful initialisation of the reset flow.

400.description: `email` is missing or invalid, or a sent `storefrontUrl` is not a domain of the shop.

post.summary: Sets a new password with the link of the recovery mail
post.description:
Last step of the password reset: sets the new password with the `hash` from the link of the recovery mail (`POST /store-api/v1/account/recovery-password`). No login needed.

The link is valid for 2 hours and only once; a new recovery mail makes the previous link invalid. After the change all sessions of the customer end, on every device. The response contains no login, continue with `POST /store-api/v1/account/login`.

The password needs at least 8 characters. Requests that send a hash are limited per IP address together with `POST /store-api/v1/account/customer-recovery-is-expired`, failed attempts count too (`429`).

hash.description: Value of the parameter `hash` from the link in the recovery mail.

newPasswordConfirm.description: Repetition of the new password, has to be equal to `newPassword`.

200.description: The password is changed and the link is used up.

400.description:
Invalid input, the field is part of the code:

- `VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/hash`: `hash` is missing or empty (`VIOLATION::INVALID_TYPE_ERROR/hash` if it is not a string).
- `VIOLATION::IS_BLANK_ERROR/newPassword`: `newPassword` is missing or empty.
- `VIOLATION::TOO_SHORT_ERROR/newPassword`: `newPassword` has less than 8 characters.
- `VIOLATION::NOT_EQUAL_ERROR/newPasswordConfirm`: `newPasswordConfirm` differs from `newPassword`.

Several errors can be returned together.

post.description: Adds products to the cart of the logged-in customer and returns the updated cart. Do not send `type`; it is always `product`. Products that do not exist are not added, the request still succeeds. Ordering needs a price: if a product (or a component of a set) has no customer price or a price on request (`999999`), no product of the request is added and the cart comes back with the notice `CHECKOUT__LINE_ITEM_BLOCKED`; a position of that product already in the cart is removed (notice `CHECKOUT__LINE_ITEM_REMOVED`). The same happens for a packaging unit that is not listed in `variants` of its product (no price, or dearer per piece than a smaller unit listed). Both notices name the product in `productId` (for a set the component without price) and come with every rejection, see `notices` of the cart. Use `available` of the stored carts to know beforehand what can be added. A customer that is not unlocked for orders gets `403` `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_PURCHASE_NOT_ALLOWED` for every product. Sending a product that is already in the cart raises the quantity of its position instead of creating a second one, also with a new `id`; the response carries the position id. Some articles are sold in several packaging units (e.g. pieces and boxes of 25); each unit is its own product. A request with exactly one product of such an article combines all cart positions of that article like a quantity change: their summed quantity goes onto the largest units listed in `variants` first, so 25 pieces become 1 box and 28 pieces 1 box and 3 pieces. Replaced positions get new ids; take them from `items` of the response. Every position that is new or has a different quantity afterwards carries the notice `CHECKOUT__UNIT_VARIANTS_COMBINED` in this response. The positions stay unchanged when the quantity does not fit the units exactly or the customer has no price for a new unit. They also stay unchanged when the request adds several products.

post.description: Places the order from the current cart and deletes the cart afterwards. Shipping address, shipping method and option, date, partial delivery, notice, reference, comment and payment method are taken from the cart; set them before with the `set-*` endpoints. The cart is validated first (`422`), then `termsAccepted` (`400`).

shopIdentifier.description: Optional. Identifier of the client, given by Strombauer. The own shop frontend and the external app each have their own; the order is recorded as shop or app order accordingly. Without an identifier or with an unknown one it is recorded as API order. An unknown identifier is no error, the order is placed anyway.

Every other cart error that blocks the order is returned as `CHECKOUT__` plus the Shopware error key in upper case, e.g. `CHECKOUT__PRODUCT_OUT_OF_STOCK` or `CHECKOUT__SALUTATION_MISSING_BILLING_ADDRESS`; `detail` is a German sentence for the customer. Validation errors of the checkout fields (e.g. `CHECKOUT__MISSING_DELIVERY_DATE`) are answered with `422`, see there. A missing `termsAccepted` or a value other than `true` is answered with `400` as well (`VIOLATION::TOS_NOT_ACCEPTED`).

post.description:
Sends the products of the current cart as a quote request instead of ordering them, and empties the cart. The request can carry an optional note. Alternative to `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` (step 5 of the order flow). The request is passed on to Strombauer, which prepares a quote from it. No endpoint lists or follows quote requests; show `requestNumber` as reference.

Only product positions are taken over, with the quantities and prices of the cart at the time of the request; the cart is emptied completely. Shipping and payment need not be set, and the cart is not validated: cart notices such as stock do not block the request. Shipping, payment, shipping date and the other checkout values of the cart are not part of the request. Only customers that are unlocked for orders can request a quote; if the request is rejected, the cart stays as it is.

get.description:
Lists products. The filters `productIds`, `numbers`, `categoryId`, `manufacturerId`, `properties` and `tag` can be combined with `sort`, `page` and `limit`. Always set `limit`. Every product and variant carries the path of its page (`seoPath`). Products with the same sort value are ordered by `id`, so paging through all pages returns every product exactly once. With exactly one `categoryId` the response lists the filter options of the category in `facets`.

`productIds` may also contain the `id` of a unit (an entry of `variants`, e.g. the unit with `productNumber` `1207.STÜCK`). Like `GET /store-api/v1/product/{productId}`, the list then returns the product the unit belongs to, with its `id`, `name` and all units in `variants`; the requested unit is the entry of `variants` with that `id`. A product requested with several of its IDs (product and units) is listed once and counted once in `total`.

`numbers` looks up a parts list in one request: the list returns the products whose `productNumber`, `ean` or `manufacturerNumber` equals one of the numbers, ignoring case and spaces around a number. The number, EAN or manufacturer number of a unit (e.g. `1207.STÜCK`) returns the product the unit belongs to, with all units in `variants`. A product matched by several numbers is listed once and counted once in `total`. A number without match adds nothing; if no number matches, the list is empty. The response does not say which number matched: compare each number (case-insensitive) with `productNumber`, `ean` and `manufacturerNumber` of the product and of its `variants`; a number found nowhere is not in the shop or not available. Set `limit` high enough for all matched products or page through the list; more than 100 different numbers return `400` with `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__TOO_MANY_NUMBERS`, so split longer parts lists into several requests.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Filters by a product tag; `code` or `label` from `GET /store-api/v1/tag`.

parameters.name: numbers
parameters.description: Filter products by product number, EAN or manufacturer number (exact match, case-insensitive, spaces around a number are ignored), also of a unit in `variants`. The number of a packaging unit the shop does not offer lists its product, but without that unit in `variants`. Pass up to 100 different numbers as a comma-separated list, e.g. `1207,4251786202546,AST04689`, or repeat the parameter as `numbers[]=<number>` for numbers that contain a comma. Repeated numbers and empty entries are ignored; an empty value means no filter. More than 100 different numbers return `400` with `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__TOO_MANY_NUMBERS/numbers`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort order of the list. A leading `-` sorts descending. The applied sort order is returned as `sort` in the response.

With exactly one `categoryId` (an ID repeated in the list counts once) the category decides: `sortings.available` of the category in `GET /category` lists the allowed fields (each in both directions), and without `sort` the list is sorted by `sortings.default`. A value whose field the category does not offer returns `400` with `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__INVALID_SORTING`. Without `categoryId` or with several different IDs all values are allowed and the list is sorted by `-popularity` without `sort`.

- `popularity`, `-popularity`: number of orders of the last 30 days that contain the product, from all customers and all order channels, without canceled orders. Each order counts once per product, regardless of quantity and unit. A set or bundle counts only for itself. `-popularity` lists the most ordered products first. The number is updated once a day and is not part of the response. Products with the same number are sorted like `-availableStock`, then by `id`.
- `name`, `-name`: product name.
- `price`, `-price`: price of the customer for one unit of the main variant (usually the piece), otherwise the list price. Products without price come last in both directions. Only for logged-in customers with a customer number that are unlocked for orders (not for a locked customer group such as „Blockiert“); otherwise `400` with `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__PRICE_SORTING_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- `availableStock`, `-availableStock`: availability. Descending lists products in stock first (larger stock of the base unit first), then products without stock but with a restock date (earliest date first), then products without stock and without restock date (stock 0 before negative stock). Ascending gives the reverse order.

Any other value gives `400` with `STROMBAUER_STORE_API__INVALID_SORTING`.

post.description:
Price list export of the logged-in company, generated asynchronously.

**Flow**

1. `POST /store-api/v1/product-file-export/start/{format}` queues a job and answers `202` with `jobId`.
2. Poll `GET /store-api/v1/product-file-export/jobs/{jobId}` until `status` is `done` or `failed` (`queued` and `running` are in progress). On `failed`, `errorCode` names the reason.
3. On `done`, fetch the file with `GET /store-api/v1/product-file-export/download/{jobId}`. The `report` lists skipped articles and notices.

All export routes require a logged-in customer (`sw-context-token`). Jobs, limits and downloads are bound to the customer number of the company.

**Formats**

The `format` parameter carries the format and, for DATANORM, the version.

| `format` | File |
|---|---|
| `datanorm_v4.0` | `DATANORM.001` (DATANORM 4.0, CP850, CRLF) |
| `datanorm_v5.0` | `DATANORM.001` (DATANORM 5.0, CP850, CRLF) |
| `csv` | `Preisliste_<customerNumber>_<YYYYMMDD>.csv` (UTF-8 with BOM, `;` separated, CRLF) |
| `pdf` | `Preisliste_<customerNumber>_<YYYYMMDD>.pdf` |

`datanorm` without a version, an unknown version or an unknown format answer `400`. The optional body field `longText` adds the product descriptions as long texts.

**Limits**

- Only one export per company at a time (all formats). A queued or running job older than the configured stale timeout (default 30 minutes) is failed automatically and no longer blocks. Otherwise `409` `STROMBAUER_EXPORT__ALREADY_RUNNING`.
- Daily limit of successful exports per customer number across all formats (default 5, counted per calendar day Europe/Berlin, failed runs do not count). Otherwise `429` `STROMBAUER_EXPORT__DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED`.
- Generated files are deleted after the configured retention period (default 14 days).

**Errors**

Errors of the export routes use the common error format (see "Errors").

Also accepts `1` and `0` and the strings `"true"`, `"false"`, `"1"` and `"0"`; `null` and an empty string count as `false`. Other values answer `400` `STROMBAUER_EXPORT__INVALID_OPTIONS`.

Customers that are not unlocked for orders get `404` `CUSTOMER__SALES_ORDER_NOT_FOUND` like for an unknown order. Each order includes sections, the progress of the order (AG-622): always RECEIPT (Eingang), INSPECTION (Prüfung) and STORAGE (Lager), each with id, German name, current (the order is in this section now) and status, the last status the order reached in the section: id (e.g. RECEIVED, WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER, PACKING; delivered by delivery option HANDED_TO_CARRIER, PICKED_UP or DELIVERED), name (description maintained in the administration), priority, color (#RRGGBB) and at (time, null while not recorded yet); the icons come once per status from GET /store-api/v1/sales-order-statuses. status is null while the section was not reached; a canceled order (nothing posted) shows only RECEIPT, a partly delivered order with canceled rest counts as delivered. A step empties the later sections: an order that goes back (e.g. from PACKING to WAITING_FOR_SUPPLIER) or is canceled no longer shows its earlier STORAGE step. Positions return orderedQuantity and canceledQuantity (null while BC may still deliver or unknown). Article positions (type Item) always have a productNumber; measureUnit is null without unit. Passed sections are completed: an order in STORAGE shows REVIEWED in INSPECTION, RECEIPT shows RECEIVED once the order is further (also replacing CANCELED when a canceled order continues). Orders not released for the customer yet (no BC state or IN EINGABE and nothing posted, also after deletion in BC) are not returned; with a posted shipment or invoice they are returned without status in the sections. The detail adds a shipping state per delivery (PREPARING, HANDED_OVER, CARRIER_DELIVERED, PICKED_UP, DELIVERED by pickup, own express delivery or carrier and CDG_Shipment_Status) and a payment state per invoice (OPEN, PAID, CANCELED from the remaining amount). There is no lifecycle state on the order; the payment state is per invoice. documents lists the PDF attachments of all documents of the order (the order itself, deliveries, invoices and credit memos; other files are left out) with id, name, extension, type, documentNumber and documentDate (date of the document: order, delivery note, invoice or credit memo date, AG-733; no size, BC does not report it reliably); deliveries and invoices carry their own attachments in the same shape. B. `RECEIVED`, `WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER`, `PACKING`; geliefert je nach Lieferoption `HANDED_TO_CARRIER` „An Versanddienstleister übergeben“, `PICKED_UP` „Abgeholt“, `DELIVERED` „Ausgeliefert“), `name` (im Admin gepflegte Beschreibung), `priority`, `color` (`#RRGGBB`) und `at` (Zeitpunkt, `null` solange nicht erfasst); die Icons kommen einmal je Status aus `GET /store-api/v1/sales-order-statuses`. Ein noch nicht erreichter Bereich hat `status: null`; ein stornierter Auftrag (nichts gebucht) zeigt nur Eingang „Storniert“, ein teilgelieferter mit storniertem Rest gilt als geliefert. Ein Schritt leert die späteren Bereiche: Geht ein Auftrag zurück (z. B. von „Wird gepackt“ auf „Warten auf Belieferung“) oder wird er storniert, zeigt Lager seinen früheren Schritt nicht mehr. Positionen liefern `orderedQuantity` und `canceledQuantity` (stornierter Rest, `null` solange BC noch liefern kann oder unbekannt). Artikelpositionen (`type` `Item`) haben immer eine `productNumber`; `measureUnit` ist `null` ohne Einheit. `items[].shipmentBlocked` (AG-862) ist `true`, wenn BC den Warenausgang der Position gesperrt hat („Warenausgang gesperrt“), sie noch einen Rest hat, zugleich eine andere Artikelposition ohne Sperre noch offen ist und der Auftrag nicht auf Komplettlieferung steht (`shipping.partialDeliveryRequested` nicht `false`): Der Rest kommt dann in einer späteren Lieferung, für die es noch kein Datum gibt, das geplante Lieferdatum gilt nur für die übrigen Positionen. Sonst `false`, auch sobald BC nichts mehr liefert. Durchlaufene Bereiche werden abgeschlossen: Steht der Auftrag in Lager, zeigt Prüfung „Geprüft“; Eingang zeigt „Eingegangen“, sobald der Auftrag weiter ist (auch statt „Storniert“, wenn ein stornierter Auftrag doch weiterläuft). Aufträge, die für Kunden noch nicht freigegeben sind (ohne BC-Status oder `IN EINGABE` und noch nichts gebucht, auch nach dem Löschen in BC), werden nicht ausgeliefert; mit gebuchter Lieferung oder Rechnung kommen sie ohne Status in den Bereichen. Für unbekannte, fremde und ausgeblendete Aufträge kommt dieselbe 404-Antwort. Jeder Lieferschein in `deliveries` hat `state` nach Versandweg und BC `CDG_Shipment_Status`: Abholung immer `PICKED_UP` „Abgeholt“; eigene Express-Lieferung immer `DELIVERED` „Ausgeliefert“ (keine Statusverfolgung); Spedition/Paketdienst `PREPARING` „Versand wird vorbereitet“, `HANDED_OVER` „An Versanddienstleister übergeben“ oder `CARRIER_DELIVERED` „Vom Versanddienstleister zugestellt“. Ein unbekannter BC-Status erscheint unverändert, ein Speditions- oder Paketlieferschein ohne Status hat `state` `null`. Jede Rechnung in `invoices` hat `state`: `CANCELED` „Storniert“, sonst `OPEN` „Offen“ (Restbetrag > 0) oder `PAID` „Bezahlt“ (Restbetrag 0). `shipping.notice` ist der Lieferhinweis des Kunden aus der Kasse (BC `CDG_Delivery_Remark`), ohne Lieferhinweis `null`. `reference` ist die Referenz des Kunden (BC „Ihre Referenz“, `Your_Reference`), `comment` sein Kommentar aus der Kasse (BC „Kommentar des Kunden“, `CDG_Customer_Comment`, AG-784), je `null` ohne Angabe. Lieferung: `shipping.partialDeliveryRequested` ist der Kundenwunsch Teillieferung (BC `Shipping_Advice`, `null` wenn unbekannt), `shipping.fullyShipped`, ob der Auftrag komplett geliefert ist (BC `Completely_Shipped`). Termine: `shipping.plannedDeliveryDate` ist das geplante Liefer- bzw. Abholdatum (BC „Geplantes Lieferdatum (SB)“), `shipping.timeWindow` die geplante Uhrzeit dazu, `shipping.plannedShipmentDate` das geplante Warenausgangsdatum. Liegt eines der beiden Daten vor heute (deutscher Kalendertag), sind alle drei `null` (überholter Plan, AG-722); ohne geplantes Lieferdatum ist `timeWindow` leer. Lieferart (AG-722): `shipping.type` wie in der Liste (`PICKUP` „Abholung“, `EXPRESS` „Lieferung durch Strombauer“, `CARRIER` „Spedition/Paketdienst“, `null` solange BC weder Versandart noch Zusteller kennt). Bei Abholung ist `shipping.address` `null`, wie im Warenkorb der Kasse. Jeder Lieferschein in `deliveries` hat zusätzlich `type` nach seiner eigenen Versandart (kann vom Auftrag abweichen, z. B. abgeholter Teil eines Lieferauftrags); ein abgeholter Lieferschein hat `shippingAddress` `null`. Positionspreise: `items[].price.unit` ist der VK-Preis aus BC, `items[].price.net` der Netto-Stückpreis nach Zeilenrabatt, auf den Cent gerundet und damit nur ein Richtwert, `items[].price.total` der Zeilenbetrag aus BC. Mit Zeilenrabatt ergibt `quantity × net` nicht immer `total`; Summen deshalb immer aus `total` bilden, nie aus `quantity × net`. Belege (AG-720): `documents` listet die PDF-Anhänge aller Belege des Auftrags in einer Liste (andere Dateien wie E-Mails oder Bilder werden nicht ausgegeben und lassen sich nicht laden), zuerst die des Auftrags selbst (z. B. Auftragsbestätigung), dann die der Lieferscheine, Rechnungen und Gutschriften. Dieselben Einträge stehen auch je Beleg unter `deliveries[].attachments` und `invoices[].attachments` (`[]` ohne Anhang); Gutschriften stehen nur in `documents`. Jeder Eintrag hat `id` (zum Laden über `GET /store-api/v1/sales-order/download/{orderId}/{documentId}`), `name` (Dateiname mit Endung), `extension` (kleingeschrieben, z. B. `pdf`, `null` ohne Endung), `type` (`ORDER` „Auftrag“, `DELIVERY` „Lieferschein“, `INVOICE` „Rechnung“, `CREDIT_MEMO` „Gutschrift“), `documentNumber` (Nummer des Belegs, z. B. `RE26-5120`) und `documentDate` (Datum des Belegs: Auftrags-, Lieferschein-, Rechnungs- bzw. Gutschriftsdatum, `Y-m-d`, `null` wenn unbekannt; AG-733). Eine Dateigröße gibt es nicht: BC meldet sie für die meisten Anhänge nicht (z. B. bei allen ZUGFeRD-Rechnungen).

get.description: Returns the sales orders of the logged-in customer, newest first by order date: all open orders, however old, and the orders with a delivery or invoice of the last twelve months; orders that change later are added as they change. Only customers unlocked for orders (`customerState: UNLOCKED` in `GET /store-api/v1/account/customer`) get their orders; for every other customer the list is empty, like for an account without customer number. The first call of a customer prepares these orders, open ones first; `syncState` says how far that is (`LOADING_OPEN`, `LOADING_HISTORY`, `DONE`, `FAILED`). While it is not `DONE`, call again every few seconds; newly prepared orders appear in the list. With `FAILED` the list may be incomplete; a later call (after five minutes at the earliest) tries again. Orders of the same date always come in the same order, so paging with `p`/`limit` never repeats or skips an order. With `term` and/or `filter` only the matching orders are returned and `total` counts them. `filterCounts` always returns the number of orders per filter (AG-721), over all orders of the customer, independent of `term` and `filter`, so clients can show "Offene Rechnungen (3)" and hide empty filters without loading the lists. Each order includes sections, the progress of the order (AG-622): always RECEIPT (Eingang), INSPECTION (Prüfung) and STORAGE (Lager), each with id, German name, current (the order is in this section now) and status, the last status the order reached in the section: id (e.g. RECEIVED, WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER, PACKING; delivered by delivery option HANDED_TO_CARRIER, PICKED_UP or DELIVERED), name (description maintained in the administration), priority, color (#RRGGBB) and at (time, null while not recorded yet); the icons come once per status from GET /store-api/v1/sales-order-statuses. status is null while the section was not reached; a canceled order (nothing posted) shows only RECEIPT, a partly delivered order with canceled rest counts as delivered. A step empties the later sections: an order that goes back (e.g. from PACKING to WAITING_FOR_SUPPLIER) or is canceled no longer shows its earlier STORAGE step. Positions return orderedQuantity and canceledQuantity (null while BC may still deliver or unknown). Article positions (type Item) always have a productNumber; measureUnit is null without unit. Passed sections are completed: an order in STORAGE shows REVIEWED in INSPECTION, RECEIPT shows RECEIVED once the order is further (also replacing CANCELED when a canceled order continues). Orders not released for the customer yet (no BC state or IN EINGABE and nothing posted, also after deletion in BC) are not returned; with a posted shipment or invoice they are returned without status in the sections. Hidden orders are neither listed nor counted in total. There is no lifecycle state on the order; the payment state is per invoice. `reference` is the customer's reference and `comment` the customer's comment from the checkout (BC `Your_Reference` and `CDG_Customer_Comment`, AG-784), each `null` without one. A newly placed order is listed once the order has been received for processing, usually within a few minutes; until then `pendingOrderCount` counts it.

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: Optional search term. Returns the orders of the customer, from any date, in which the term is part of the order number (`number`, e.g. `AUF26-9217`), the shop order number (`externalOrderNumber`), the reference (`reference`) or the article number or article name of a line item. Upper and lower case are ignored. Line items are matched by the article number and name recorded with the order; `items[].productNumber` and `items[].name` show the current shop data, which can differ slightly (e.g. `1723.STÜCK` is found by `1723`). Leading and trailing spaces are ignored; an empty term returns all orders as without the parameter.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Optional filters (AG-721), several separated by commas (`filter=OPEN_INVOICES,ACTION_REQUIRED`) or as list (`filter[]=OPEN_INVOICES&filter[]=ACTION_REQUIRED`). With several filters an order must match all of them; combinable with `term` and `p`/`limit`. Filters run over all orders of the customer, from any date (an open invoice of last year is still open). `OPEN_INVOICES` „Offene Rechnungen“: at least one invoice with `state` `OPEN` (remaining amount > 0; canceled invoices never count); the payment state is as current as the last invoice sync from Business Central. `OPEN_DELIVERIES` „Offene Lieferungen“: BC still delivers the order and an article position (`type` `Item`) has an undelivered rest, `orderedQuantity` − `shippedQuantity` > 0 (nothing is canceled while BC still delivers), including orders nothing has been shipped of yet. Positions without `orderedQuantity` (orders not synchronised since 16.10.2026) do not count, because the rest is unknown. Once BC delivers nothing more, the rest is canceled (`canceledQuantity`) and the order no longer counts. `ACTION_REQUIRED` „Wartet auf dich“: the current status (the `status` of the section with `current: true`) is `WAITING_FOR_CUSTOMER`, `WAITING_FOR_PREPAYMENT` or `WAITING_FOR_CREDIT_LIMIT`. Values are upper case; blanks, tabs and line breaks around a value and empty values are ignored, an empty parameter means no filter. Any other value, also control characters, answers 400 `CUSTOMER__SALES_ORDER_INVALID_FILTER`.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Page number (starts at 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of orders per page (maximum 100).

Sonst `false`, auch sobald BC nichts mehr liefert. Durchlaufene Bereiche werden abgeschlossen: Steht der Auftrag in Lager, zeigt Prüfung „Geprüft“; Eingang zeigt „Eingegangen“, sobald der Auftrag weiter ist (auch statt „Storniert“, wenn ein stornierter Auftrag doch weiterläuft). Aufträge, die für Kunden noch nicht freigegeben sind (ohne BC-Status oder `IN EINGABE` und noch nichts gebucht, auch nach dem Löschen in BC), werden nicht ausgeliefert; mit gebuchter Lieferung oder Rechnung kommen sie ohne Status in den Bereichen. Ausgeblendete Aufträge zählen nicht zu `total`. Lieferart (AG-722): `shipping.type` sagt, ob der Auftrag abgeholt oder geliefert wird: `PICKUP` „Abholung“, `EXPRESS` „Lieferung durch Strombauer“ (eigene Lokallieferung) oder `CARRIER` „Spedition/Paketdienst“; `null`, solange BC weder Versandart noch Zusteller kennt. Full-text search for products, e.g. for a search result page. The filters `productIds`, `categoryId`, `manufacturerId`, `properties` and `tag` can be added. The results are sorted by relevance to the term, results with the same relevance by `id`. Filters do not change the order, so paging through all pages returns every product exactly once. The term is searched in name, product number, manufacturer number, variant number and EAN. A term that is a single word with at least three characters and a digit is also found as a part of a number (`SMR032` finds `SMR032-ASA00828`, `613` finds `1613`); the EAN is found only as a whole. A term also matches the beginning of a word of the name (`h3` finds `FoxEss H3-10K-Smart`). A word of at least four characters also matches a part of the manufacturer name (`solar` finds the products of `Trina Solar`). Typos in words of the name are corrected: a word of at least five letters may have one wrong, missing or extra letter or two swapped neighbouring letters, a word of at least ten letters two of them; a wrong first letter and terms containing a digit are not corrected. With several words a product needs to match only one of them; products matching more of them come first. A number of a variant returns its main product. `total` counts all hits, independent of `limit`. Every product and variant carries the path of its page (`seoPath`). With exactly one `categoryId` the response lists the filter options of the category in `facets`. The response contains `searchLogId` for searches sent with `source`: report clicks on the shown products with `POST /store-api/v1/search-log/click/{searchLogId}`. Send the same `sw-context-token` with all searches and clicks of a visit.

shipmentBlocked.description: `true` if BC blocks the goods-out of the position (AG-862), it still has a rest, another article position without block is open as well and the order is not set to complete delivery (`shipping.partialDeliveryRequested` not `false`): the rest comes in a later delivery without a date yet, the planned delivery date only applies to the other positions. `false` otherwise, also once BC delivers nothing more.

total.description: Number of orders over all pages. With `term` and/or `filter` the number of orders matching all of them; hidden orders are never counted.

filterCounts.description: Number of orders of the customer per filter of `filter` (AG-721), over all orders of the list and independent of `term` and `filter`. Always contains all three keys, 0 without match. While `syncState` is not `DONE` the numbers can still grow.

OPEN_INVOICES.description: Orders with at least one open invoice („Offene Rechnungen“).

OPEN_DELIVERIES.description: Orders with a remaining quantity BC still delivers („Offene Lieferungen“).

ACTION_REQUIRED.description: Orders whose current status waits for the customer („Wartet auf dich“).

pendingOrderCount.description: Number of the customer's orders placed in the last 60 minutes that have not been received for processing yet and are therefore not in `items`; canceled orders are not counted. The same for every `term`, `filter` and page, and 0 for customers that get the empty list. An order is no longer counted once it has been received for processing, usually within a few minutes, and 60 minutes after it was placed at the latest. It is then listed, unless it is not released yet (see the description of this endpoint).

syncState.description: How far the orders of the customer are prepared (AG-743). The first call of the list starts it. `LOADING_OPEN`: open orders are still being added, newest first. `LOADING_HISTORY`: all open orders are there, orders with a delivery or invoice of the last twelve months are still being added. `DONE`: complete; customers without customer number get `DONE` right away. `FAILED`: preparing stopped, the list may be incomplete; a call after five minutes at the earliest tries again. While not `DONE`, call the list again every few seconds.

listPrice.description: Net list price of the position (price for all customers at quantity 1), to show struck through next to `price`. Set only when `price.unit` is below `listPrice.unit`. `null` for sets and bundles, for articles without a price for all customers, for guests and customers who cannot see prices, when the cart shows gross prices and when the customer's price is not lower.

selected.description: Current checkout values. `shippingAddress` has the same fields as the addresses in `available.shippingAddressId.options`, including `type`. `shippingMethodId` and `paymentMethodId` are `null` when the method stored in the context is not (or no longer) contained in the corresponding `available` list, e.g. because the cart changed; the client must then let the customer choose again. `shippingAddress` is `null` when the stored address is not contained in `available.shippingAddressId.options` because the selected shipping method does not deliver there. The shipping method then stays selected as long as it delivers to at least one other address of the customer; the client must let the customer choose one of the listed addresses. Until then `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` rejects the order with `CHECKOUT__SHIPPING_METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE`. `shippingDate` is `null` when the stored date is no longer possible: the earliest date (`available.shippingDate.earliest`) moves with the time of day, so a date chosen in the morning can be too early in the afternoon. `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` rejects such a date with `422` `CHECKOUT__INVALID_DELIVERY_DATE`; let the customer choose a new date. `shippingOptionId` is the option that applies: the chosen one, or the only option of the shipping method, which applies without a choice and is not listed in `available`. `partialDelivery` is `complete` as soon as the cart no longer offers partial delivery (the product is in stock again or was removed): a chosen `partial` then expires, also for the order, and has to be chosen again if a product runs out of stock later. `shippingAddOns` maps the ID of every add-on the selected shipping option offers to its value (`true` booked, `false` not booked); values the customer has not set yet are the add-on defaults. It is `null` when no shipping option applies or the option offers no add-ons.

available.description: Choices per checkout field. Every field has `required` and `type`. Fields with a choice list it under `options`: shipping and payment methods with `id`, `name` and `description`, shipping options with `id`, `name` and `description` (hint for the option, `null` if none is set), partial delivery with `id` and `name` (`partialDelivery` lists `partial` and is `required` only while a product of the cart is out of stock; otherwise only `complete` is listed and `required` is `false`), shipping addresses with `id`, `default`, the address fields and `type` (`billing` for the billing address, `shipping` for every other address, like in `GET /store-api/v1/account/customer`). The billing address can be selected as shipping address, but it cannot be changed or deleted. `shippingAddressId.options` only contains the addresses the selected shipping method delivers to, e.g. for local delivery only the addresses within its delivery area; the other addresses can be selected with another shipping method. `termsAccepted` has the type `boolean`: send `termsAccepted: true` with `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order`. `shippingMethodId.options` and `paymentMethodId.options` only contain the methods available for the current cart and customer; payment methods also depend on the selected shipping method. Both lists start with the default method of the shop, followed by the other methods in a fixed order. They are recalculated with every cart response and may be empty. Only fields that apply to the selected shipping method are listed: for pickup there is no `shippingAddressId`, and `selected.shippingAddress` is `null`. `shippingOptionId` is only listed, and then required, when the shipping method has at least two options; a single option applies without a choice and is reported in `selected.shippingOptionId`. `shippingAddOns` (type `booleanMap`, never required) lists the optional services of the selected shipping option (e.g. forklift, phone notice) in display order, with `id`, `name`, `description` (`null` if none is set), `price` (net amount in EUR, `null` if there is no price) and `defaultValue`; it is left out when the option offers none. Set a value with `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/set-shipping-add-on`. Show only the fields contained in `available`.

vat.description: VAT per rate. Empty for a tax-free cart: then show no VAT line at all, also not 0 %.

gross.description: Total including VAT; equals `net` for a tax-free cart.

savings.description: Net amount the customer saves against the list prices: sum of `listPrice.total` − `price.total` over all positions with `listPrice`, rounded to two decimals. `null` when no position has a list price.

taxExemption.description:
Why the cart is tax-free, `null` when it is not (AG-732). Show `message` next to the totals as long as the field is set; decide by `code`.

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INTRA_COMMUNITY_DELIVERY` | The delivery goes to an EU country other than Germany and the customer has a VAT ID of that country (e.g. `ATU…` for Austria), whatever the billing country: no German VAT. |

notices.description:
Messages about the last cart change. A message without `productId` is shown once per context; notices with `productId` come with every rejection or change, also repeated ones. Show `message` to the customer and decide by `code`, never by the wording of `message`.

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CHECKOUT__LINE_ITEM_BLOCKED` | A product of the request cannot be ordered: it has no price for the customer, its price is on request, or it is a packaging unit that is not listed in `variants` of its product. Nothing of the request was added; do not show the products as added. `productId` is that product; for a set it is the component that cannot be ordered, not the set. |
| `CHECKOUT__LINE_ITEM_REMOVED` | A position was removed from the cart because its product has no price (any more), is a packaging unit that is no longer listed in `variants` of its product, or became unavailable. `productId` is the product of that position. |
| `CHECKOUT__UNIT_VARIANTS_COMBINED` | Level `0`, the cart stays orderable. The quantity of an article was moved onto its packaging units, largest first (e.g. 25 pieces became 1 box), after `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/cart/line-item` or a quantity change. One notice per position that was created or got another quantity; `productId` is the product of that position. Only in the response of that request. |
| `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_PURCHASE_NOT_ALLOWED` | The customer is not unlocked for orders (`customerState: LOCKED` in `GET /store-api/v1/account/customer`), but the cart still has products from before the lock. The positions stay; `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` is rejected with the same code. |
| `CHECKOUT__GERMAN_VAT_ID_REQUIRED` | The billing address is outside Germany, the delivery goes to Germany and the customer has no German VAT ID (AG-732). `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` is rejected with the same code; let the customer choose a delivery address in the billing country. |
| `CHECKOUT__DELIVERY_COUNTRY_VAT_ID_REQUIRED` | The delivery goes to an EU country other than Germany and the customer has no VAT ID of that country (AG-732). `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` is rejected with the same code; let the customer choose a delivery address in Germany. |
| `CHECKOUT__SHIPPING_METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `CHECKOUT__PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE` | The selected shipping or payment method is not available for the current cart; same codes as `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order`. |

All other notices get `CHECKOUT__` plus the error key of the shop, e.g. `CHECKOUT__PRODUCT_OUT_OF_STOCK`, the same code `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/order` reports when the notice blocks the order. Show `message` for codes you do not know.

A missing login never comes as a notice: `POST /store-api/v1/checkout/cart/line-item` answers `401` with the error `CHECKOUT__CUSTOMER_LOGIN_REQUIRED`, and the cart of a guest has no notice for it.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable code of the notice (see the table above).

productId.description: Product the notice is about, `null` when it concerns no single product.

listProperties.description: Properties to show on the product cards of this category's product list, in this order, e.g. `Leistung: 475 Wp / Farbe: Full-Black / Aufbau: Glas-Glas`. Take the values from the `properties` of each product: the entry whose `propertyId` equals `id`. Skip a property the product does not have. A category without own selection uses the selection of its direct parent category (one level only, e.g. `PV-Module > Aiko` shows the properties of `PV-Module`). Empty list when neither has a selection, never `null`. Always present in `GET /category`. Only for the product lists of a category, not for search results.

filterProperties.description: Properties to offer as filters in the product list of this category, in this order. Send the selected values as `properties` to `GET /product` or `GET /search` together with `categoryId`; the values with their product counts come in `facets`. A category without own selection uses the selection of the nearest parent category that has one, over all levels. Empty list when none has a selection, never `null`. Always present in `GET /category`.

seoPath.description: Current path of the category page, without leading `/` and with `/` at the end, e.g. `Zubehoer/Solarkabel/`. Present in every entry of `GET /category`; `null` when the category has no page path. `GET /store-api/v1/seo-path` tells which page the path shows.

SVG icons (`image/svg+xml`) are single coloured with `currentColor` and a square `viewBox` without margin: draw them inline in the colour of the tile, row or active state. StrombauerProduct.description: Kompaktes Produkt für Listen. `productType` kennzeichnet Einzelprodukte (`PRODUCT`), Sets ohne eigenen Bundle-Preis (`SET`) und Bundles mit eigenem Bundle-Preis (`BUNDLE`). Bei `SET` und `BUNDLE` enthält `bundleProducts` die enthaltenen Produkte. Alle Produktlisten (`/product`, `/search`, auch mit `categoryId`, `manufacturerId`, `tag` oder `productIds`) liefern dieselben Felder.

seoPath.description: Current path of the product page, without leading `/`, e.g. `Gewerbewechselrichter/Sungrow-SG-50-CX-P2/1006`. Build the link from it; `GET /store-api/v1/seo-path` resolves it back to the product. `null` when the product has no page path.

variants.description: Packaging units of the product the shop offers; prices and stock are given per unit. A unit without a price is left out, and so is a unit that costs more per piece than the next smaller unit listed, e.g. a container that is dearer per piece than a pallet. A unit with the same price per piece stays, and a unit with a price on request stays. If no unit has a price, all units are listed. Which units are listed depends on the prices of the customer; guests and customers not unlocked for orders see the units that result from the general prices, without prices.

ean.description: EAN of this unit; a unit without its own EAN has the EAN of the product.

manufacturerNumber.description: Manufacturer number of this unit; a unit without its own manufacturer number has the one of the product.

availableStock.description: Verfügbarer Bestand dieser Variante beziehungsweise Verpackungseinheit. Für Gäste und nicht freigeschaltete Kunden (z. B. Kundengruppe „Blockiert“) ist der Wert null.

calculatedPrice.description: Netto-Staffelpreise dieser Variante beziehungsweise Verpackungseinheit als Map `{ mengenSchwelle: nettoPreis }`. Für die bestellte Menge gilt der Preis der größten MengenSchwelle, die kleiner oder gleich der Menge ist. Beispiel: Bei `{"1": 37, "10": 36, "20": 35}` gilt ab 1 Stück 37, ab 10 Stück 36 und ab 20 Stück 35. Für Gäste und nicht freigeschaltete Kunden (z. B. Kundengruppe „Blockiert“) ist der Wert leer (`[]`).

referencePrice.description: Net price per `referenceUnit` for every tier of `calculatedPrice`, as map `{ quantityThreshold: netPrice }`: price of the tier ÷ (`measureUnit.quantityPerUnit` × quantity of one piece in `referenceUnit`, e.g. 475 for a module with the value `475 Wp` in `properties`); without `measureUnit` the divisor is the quantity of one piece. Not rounded, format it like a price. Example: module with 475 Wp, piece at 100 → `{"1": 0.2105263157894737}`. Empty (`[]`) when `referenceUnit` is `null` or `calculatedPrice` is empty (e.g. for guests). A tier with the price-on-request placeholder `999999` gets no entry; all other thresholds are those of `calculatedPrice`.

listPrice.description: Net price of one unit for all customers at quantity 1, to show struck through next to the customer's price `calculatedPrice["1"]`. Set only when the customer has an own price for this unit that is below it. `null` for guests and customers who cannot see prices, for customers without an own price for the unit, for sets and bundles (`productType` `SET` or `BUNDLE`), for articles without a price for all customers and when the customer's price is not lower. `listPrice` is not present when `calculatedPrice` is grouped by unit code (a product with several units and no variant per unit). Use the values of the variant of that unit from another response.

stockForecast.description: Forecast of the available quantity of this unit, as map `{ "YYYY-MM-DD": quantity }` in order of the day. Lists only the days on which the quantity changes; a quantity applies until the next listed day. The forecast covers the next 30 days. If the unit has no stock in these days but a delivery is expected, it continues up to 30 days after the delivery and ends with an extra entry for its last day, with the same quantity as the entry before. For guests and customers that are not unlocked (e.g. customer group „Blockiert“) the value is null.

seoPath.description: Current path of the page of this packaging unit, without leading `/`. Link it to open the product with this unit selected. `null` when the unit has no own page path; use the `seoPath` of the product then.

Dank IP66- und Korrosionsschutzklasse C5, IEC-Schutzbaugruppen bis Typ I+II (DC) und Typ II (AC) sowie integriertem Überspannungsschutz bietet er hohe Betriebssicherheit. Merkmale wie PID‑Recovery, dynamische Verschattungskompensation, Smart-IV-Curve-Diagnose und integrierter Netzstörungsdatenlogger ermöglichen effiziente Inbetriebnahme und Fernwartung. id.description: Delivery: PREPARING, HANDED_OVER, CARRIER_DELIVERED, PICKED_UP, DELIVERED (or an unknown BC shipping status as it is). Invoice: OPEN, PAID, CANCELED.

BcOrderDetailResponse.description: The fields of a list entry (`BcOrdersResponse.items`) plus totals, shipping, payment, deliveries, invoices and documents.

sections.description: Progress of the order: always RECEIPT, INSPECTION and STORAGE, in this order.

shipping.description: The fields of `SalesOrderShippingSummary` (`type`, `plannedDeliveryDate`, `timeWindow`) plus `partialDeliveryRequested`, `fullyShipped`, `condition`, `carrier`, `service`, `addOns`, `tailLift` and `b2cDelivery` (both deprecated), `requestedDate`, `plannedShipmentDate` (`null` like the planned delivery date once the plan is outdated), `notice` and `address` (`null` for a pickup).

addOns.description: Booked shipping add-ons (e.g. „Hebebühne“), in the order of the shop's add-on list; `[]` if none is booked (AG-626).

name.description: Name of the add-on as offered in the checkout.

tailLift.description: Lifting platform booked; `false` if unknown. Deprecated: use `addOns`.

b2cDelivery.description: B2C delivery booked; `false` if unknown. Deprecated: use `addOns`.

deliveries.description: Posted shipments as stored from BC, each with its computed shipping state, its delivery type and its attachments; a picked-up shipment has `shippingAddress` `null`.

attachments.description: Attachments of this delivery, `[]` without attachment.

invoices.description: Posted invoices as stored from BC, each with its computed payment state and its attachments.

attachments.description: Attachments of this invoice, `[]` without attachment.

documents.description: PDF attachments of all documents of the order: first those of the order itself, then those of the deliveries, invoices and credit memos (AG-720). Other files (e.g. e-mails, images) are left out.

SalesOrderDeliveryType.description: Whether a sales order or delivery is picked up or delivered, and how (AG-722); `null` while BC knows neither shipment method nor shipping agent.

id.description: PICKUP: the customer picks the goods up. EXPRESS: Strombauer delivers itself (local delivery). CARRIER: forwarder or parcel service.

SalesOrderShippingSummary.description: Delivery type and planned date of a sales order (AG-722), in the list and as part of `shipping` in the detail.

plannedDeliveryDate.description: Planned delivery date, for a pickup the planned pickup date (BC „Geplantes Lieferdatum (SB)“). `null` without plan or once the planned goods-out or delivery date lies before today (German calendar day).

timeWindow.description: Planned time of the planned date; both `null` without planned date.

SalesOrderDocument.description: Attachment of a document of a sales order from Business Central (AG-720). Download it with `GET /store-api/v1/sales-order/download/{orderId}/{documentId}`. There is no file size: BC reports none for most attachments (e.g. every ZUGFeRD invoice).

id.description: Attachment ID for the download, as BC delivers it (lowercase with hyphens).

name.description: File name with extension, also the name of the download; `null` if BC has none.

extension.description: Lowercase extension of `name`; always `pdf`, other files are not listed.

type.description: Kind of document the attachment belongs to.

documentNumber.description: Number of the document the attachment belongs to (order, delivery, invoice or credit memo number).

documentDate.description: Date of the document the attachment belongs to: order date, delivery note date, invoice date or credit memo date (Y-m-d); `null` if unknown. Use this date to show when the document was issued (AG-733).

icon.description: Image data URL of at most 20 KB; render as image only, never inline. `null` without icon.

StrombauerSeoPath.description: Page a path of the shop shows. Fields that do not belong to the `type` are left out.

type.description:
Kind of page and what to load for it:

- `product`: product detail, `GET /store-api/v1/product/{id}`.
- `category`: category page, products with `categoryId` = `id`.
- `manufacturer`: manufacturer page, products with `manufacturerId` = `id`.
- `group`: product group of the category `id`, products with `categoryId` = `id`; `tagCodes` names the tags of the group.
- `categoryManufacturer`: one manufacturer within a category, products with `categoryId` and `manufacturerId`.

id.description: Product ID for `product`, category ID for `category`, `group` and `categoryManufacturer`, manufacturer ID for `manufacturer`.

canonicalPath.description: Current path of the page, without leading `/`. If it differs from the requested path (old path, other upper and lower case), redirect to it permanently and use it as canonical link.

categoryId.description: Only for `categoryManufacturer`: the category whose products are shown.

manufacturerId.description: Only for `categoryManufacturer`: the manufacturer the products are filtered by.

tagCodes.description: Only for `group`: codes of the tags whose products the group shows, sorted. Load the products of the group with `categoryId` = `id`; a single code works as `tag` filter of `GET /store-api/v1/product`.

400.description: Bad Request.

errors.detail: Die Anfrage enthält eine ungültige Kennung.

401.description: Unauthorized: no customer is logged in, or the login data is wrong.
